correctness.rationale: Each output word corresponds to a path in the sixteen-state labeled input graph; accessible output words are counted exactly by the reachable-subset deterministic matrix, so topological entropy is the logarithm of its Perron root. Executing the packaged verifier recomputed all sixteen exact matrices and characteristic polynomials, established seven disjoint rational Perron intervals using exact Sturm root counts, confirmed the shared fixed-SFT Perron factor, and checked all sixteen nine-input-bit idempotence decisions. An independent C99 exhaustive direct-word enumerator agreed for all sixteen rules and lengths zero through ten. Bit complement conjugacy covers the other sixteen rules. The infinite word result follows from finite-state path counting and Perron–Frobenius theory, not from finite test samples.

The published erosion result handles a special spatial pattern and filtration and does not imply the full classification.

value.rationale: The complete 32-rule single-active-neighborhood radius-two class is natural, smallest beyond elementary three-input rules. Seven exact one-step spatial-entropy classes and their populations address a finite but nontrivial dynamical invariant. Crucially the twelve non-idempotent rules share the same fixed-point entropy yet have exactly two strictly larger first-image entropies, clarifying a concrete structural gap between one-step information preservation and fixed-state language. This result does not merely reprove the idempotence dichotomy or list an arbitrary small subset.
